content.text:
**Read another sheet:** pass `sheet` to `read_xlsx` (default is the first sheet):

```sql
SELECT * FROM read_xlsx('/home/uploads/2026-01-31/budget.xlsx', sheet = 'FY26') LIMIT 20
```

That’s already in the excel skill example.

**List all sheet names:** DuckDB has no API for that yet ([open request](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-excel/issues/54)). Options:

1. **Sandbox (preferred)** — what the skill already teaches:

```python
import pandas as pd
book = pd.ExcelFile("files/uploads/2026-01-31/budget.xlsx")
print(book.sheet_names)
```

2. **Hack via a bad sheet name** — DuckDB’s error lists available sheets:

```sql
SELECT * FROM read_xlsx('budget.xlsx', sheet = '__missing__')
-- Binder Error: Sheet "__missing__" not found ...
-- Did you mean: "Sheet1", "FY26", ...
```

So: use SQL when you already know the sheet name; use the sandbox (or that error hack) when you need discovery.

Done. Both pieces are in and the backend suite is green (except a pre-existing OIDC allowlist test failure that's unrelated to this work).

## 1. Skills are now rendered per run, with sandbox content hidden when there is no sandbox

`InternalSkill.body` went from a precomputed string to `(capabilities: SkillCapabilities) => string`, and `load_skill` computes the capabilities from the run:

```25:29:apps/backend/src/agents/tools/load-skill.ts
/** Mirrors how the tool set itself is assembled, so a skill only offers tools the run really has. */
const skillCapabilities = (context: ToolContext | undefined): SkillCapabilities => {
	return { canRunSandbox: isSandboxAvailable && context?.agentSettings?.experimental?.sandboxes === true };
};
```

That mirrors exactly how `getTools` decides to include `execute_sandboxed_code` (runtime installed **and** the experimental setting on). To import the availability flag without dragging the whole sandbox tool — and its `bun:sqlite` transitive import — into the skill path, the boxlite probe moved to `src/services/sandbox-runtime.ts`; `execute-sandboxed-code.ts` re-exports `isSandboxAvailable` from there, so nothing else changed.

The excel skill without a sandbox no longer mentions pandas, openpyxl, `storage_files` or `save_files` anywhere; instead it gets the DuckDB equivalent of each thing pandas was there for: peeking at the raw grid with `range` + `header = false` + `all_varchar`, then reading with an explicit range, `empty_as_varchar` / `ignore_errors` for dirty columns, a `last_value(... IGNORE NULLS)` window to fill a merged grouping column down, `TRY_CAST`/`strptime` for types, and "save a CSV, and do not promise a workbook you cannot write" instead of `ExcelWriter`. The pdf skill got the same treatment (no pdfplumber section, no OCR offer). A registry test asserts no skill body mentions a sandbox when `canRunSandbox` is false, so this can't quietly regress.

## 2. `read` on an .xlsx returns the workbook's tabs and their shape

New `src/services/workbook.ts` inflates only `xl/workbook.xml`, the workbook rels, and each sheet part's declared `<dimension>` (via `fflate`, added as a backend dependency, with a decompression budget so a zip bomb can't blow up memory). Cells are never touched. `toReadableText` routes `.xlsx` there, so it works for uploads and project-folder files alike, and `read` on a project file now dispatches on `isBinaryDocument` rather than a `.pdf` special case. Real output, on a workbook openpyxl wrote:

```
1:Excel workbook with 3 sheets, in tab order. No cells are read here: query a sheet by name with the local database, e.g. SELECT * FROM read_xlsx('<path>', sheet = 'Cover') LIMIT 20.
2:- 'Cover' — 3 rows × 1 column (A1:A3)
3:- 'FY26 & FY27' — 203 rows × 3 columns (A1:C203)
4:- 'Archive' (hidden) — 1 row × 1 column (A1:A1)
5:The counts are the used range the file records, so they include any title, blank or totals rows around the table — look at the first rows before deciding where the header is.
```

Hidden sheets are flagged, XML-escaped names come back as Excel shows them, a sheet with no declared range says so rather than inventing a size, and a non-zip or encrypted file fails with "corrupt or password-protected". Verified against openpyxl- and xlsxwriter-written workbooks, not just the test fixture.

Three places now point the agent at it: the saved-files section of the system prompt, the local-database section (`read_xlsx` reads the first sheet unless you pass `sheet = 'Name'`, and `read` lists the names), and the attachment line itself when the file is an `.xlsx`.

One design note worth your call: the outline is on demand, not pushed. I chose that over computing it at upload time and injecting it into every message, since it costs nothing until the agent looks and needs no schema change — but if you'd rather the sheet list always be in context (or shown in the UI next to the attachment chip), that's a different, larger change and I'd do it at upload time in the message part.

The error count of 3 came from lines with "error" in the strings, and all the warnings are pre-existing in files I didn't modify. Now I need to update the todo list and write up a summary covering how skills now render with their capabilities per run, with sandbox content hidden when there's no sandbox environment like with Excel and PDF files.

I've also wired in the xlsx file reading to return a workbook outline showing sheets, hidden status, and used ranges—this integrates with the file-text system, works for both home and project files, and ties into the system prompt and skill guidance. Added the new fflate dependency and tests for it. There's a pre-existing OIDC test that's still failing, and I should note the alternative approach of computing metadata at upload time that I didn't go with in case they prefer that instead. I'll list out the changed files in readable prose format.
